name: Build Your Own Future
author: Multiverse Video editors
description: Replace dependence on opaque platforms with skills and infrastructure you control.

items.note: Framasoft's short, translated explainer of the Fediverse: many independent servers that talk to each other, like email.
Framasoft's two-minute explainer of PeerTube, the federated video platform this app reads from, with subtitles in 30+ languages.
A LibrePlanet 2024 talk on self-hosting that lasts: how to save, serve and safely back up your own data for years, not weekends.
The story of B4RN, a community-built fibre network in rural England that has connected over 7,000 homes through joint action, with captions.
From Battlemesh v15: how the COWMesh community network brought connectivity to a rural area in India, built and run by locals.
curl maintainer Daniel Stenberg at foss-north 2026 on what AI tools are really doing to open-source projects, from someone on the receiving end.
A talk on the Open Source AI Definition one year on: which 'open' models really are, and how to spot open-washing.
A CounterSpy conference talk from the Co-op Cloud project on platform surveillance and how cooperatives can run their own infrastructure instead.
Build a chatbot character inside a Godot game that talks to a language model running on your own machine through Ollama.
Lessons from building a networking stack for microcontrollers with 32 kB of RAM, in Go.
One short lesson from Techlore's free Go Incognito course: what actually protects your traffic on a network, and what doesn't.
From the Blender Conference 2026: procedural workflows with Gaussian splatting, the new way to turn photos into 3D scenes.
Cory Doctorow's talk The Post-American Internet, posted with captions by Framasoft: an argument for interoperability as the way out of platform lock-in.
A long conversation with Evan Prodromou, an architect of ActivityPub, the protocol behind the Fediverse, on why it was built for people first.
The Bonfire project on federated digital spaces built for mutual aid networks, as an alternative to running them on corporate group chats.
A FOSS4G talk on interactive open-source tools for visualizing climate risk, used in disaster-reduction programmes.
A LibrePlanet 2023 panel on why mainstream platforms are free of charge, what that costs the Global South, and what a libre alternative looks like.
Grant makers and builders debate who should fund technology that's given away for free, and which tech deserves public money.
A NorthSec talk on fitting threat modeling into fast development cycles, so security questions get asked while the design can still change.
A persuasive case that everyone should run a home server, or have a friend who does, and what that buys you.
Veronica Explains pushes back on tech's habit of shaming people's hardware and software choices: your tools are probably fine.
A Hackerspace Brussels talk on using free software to build your own autonomous robots.
A short interview on why teams are self-hosting their design tools, using Penpot as the example.
